last.desc: We look forward to camping with you are Camp Emerald Bay in the Summer of 2027! Please read everything below prior to registering. Required Information You can make your registration without including participant information. You can also add information for just one or two of your participants and come back to add in more. Do not use placeholder information. If you don't have all required information, leave spaces blank and click continue at the bottom of the page. You will need first name, last name, BSA ID, birthday, dietary restrictions, and T-Shirt size for each participant. Email and phone number are required for participants participating in Lifeguard courses. T-Shirts are not included in the cost of camp. Pricing Pricing is subject to change based on remaining capacity. The price if you register today is listed below and is the price any future added participants will also pay. A deposit of $800 is required to apply. Registrations without a deposit made will be held for 14 days and then deleted. The deposit is applied to the registration balance. The only accepted methods of payment are E-Check through Doubleknot and check mailed to our Council Office, with the reservation or order number in the memo line. Payment Schedule – Payments must be postmarked by the following dates Due with initial registration is an $800 non-refundable deposit that applies to the troop’s overall balance. January 8th, 2027 - $250 per participant (including adults) is due. March 5th, 2027 - $250 per participant is due. May 12th, 2027 - Remaining balance is due. Including all program fees. Remaining balance to be paid on last day at camp. Activity Sign Up Merit Badge and Activity Sign Ups will be available starting April 1st at 10am. We don’t cap most classes. The only classes with caps are American Red Cross Lifeguard, Sailing, Pottery, and Marine Science courses. You may drop into classes once at camp by going to the class you want to participate in. Rugged Adventures and SCUBA Certification programs Register all participants, and in the “What are they doing” section, you can select Rugged Adventure Programs for your campers. Pay attention to the schedule of Rugged Adventures program on the website. SCUBA Events are signed up for using a separate SCUBA form. It can be found on the website starting in September. SCUBA event fees are non refundable and subject to In2Deep Diving's policies. Refund and Cancellation Policy – Share with each participant REFUNDS - Western Los Angeles County Council has a NO REFUND Policy for summer camp reservation payments. HOW MANY TO REGISTER? - Please do not reserve more spaces than you can guarantee to fill. But do not count on adding more spaces later as our weeks do fill up and we may not be able to accommodate your whole troop if you underestimate. Get commitment from participants early. Once the balance is paid in full, refunds will not be issued if participants drop. RESERVATION CHANGES - Increases in numbers can be made until camp is full, at which point you will not be able to make those changes. Decreases in numbers are allowed until the final payment deadline or your registration is paid in full. However, no refunds will be given if the decrease in participants means your registration will have a credit balance even before full payment. Please email us for requests to change your registration, or fill out the registration change request form found on the website. CHANGES CONT. – If you need to swap participants, let us know. We can make swaps of participants at any point, even once the registration is paid in full. WAITLIST – If a week becomes full, contact us to be put on the waitlist. We make a decision on whether to add people from the waitlist in about two weeks. CANCELLATIONS - Cancellation of a whole reservation will result in forfeiture of any payments made. DEPOSIT - A non-refundable, non-transferable deposit is required to apply. Registrations without a deposit made will be held for 14 days and then deleted. This deposit will only be returned if no space is available. The deposit is applied to the registration balance. LATE PAYMENTS - We reserve the right to charge a fee of 10% of the required payment amount to be applied if payments are not received within 2 weeks of payment deadlines. CIRCUMSTANCES THAT WARRANT REFUNDS: If we are unable to provide the program for any reason, troops will be offered to switch to a different week, a future summer event at a WLACC Summer Camp, or given a full refund. Medical and other refunds requests will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis and documentation will be required as a part of the request. All refund requests must be submitted via email to camping@bsa-la.org and they take 6-8 weeks to process once approved. The funds will be sent to the registration owner. For Provisional Campers (Groups of campers without two deep leadership) If your registration includes just one participant, Doubleknot will ask you to pay in full if registering after January, you can select Pay By Mail at check out to pay with check, or pay in full at a later date. You are considered provisional if your registration doesn’t include at least two adults. Your group will be assigned to camp with another troop with plenty of adults.

last.desc: San Diego Imperial Council presents COPE What is Project COPE? COPE is an acronym for Challenging Outdoor Personal Experience and at Mataguay Scout Ranch, we have a weekend that will do just that! Whether your unit needs help learning how to Communicate, Plan, Trust each other, Team-work, build Leadership, learn to Make Decisions, Problem Solve, or just build Self-esteem, we have a program that will fill your unit’s needs. For units that wish to camp as a part of their experience, camping is under the high course and is “backpack” style. Initiative Games Our staff works with your unit through initiative games and objectives that help get everyone in the mood for the day's activities. These "simple" games combined with unit leaders input help identify where your group could use guidance and improvement throughout the weekend. Low Course The Low Course is where your group begins to shine. Through numerous elements (between 18” and 12 feet off the ground) we begin to challenge your group to think outside the box, grow their leadership skills and work cohesively. Each objective builds upon the previous tasks and presents new and exciting challenges. Some groups that enter the program complete all the elements, however most do not. Remember that even if your group has been through a Low Course on previous adventures, we can tailor your weekend to give your unit a chance to achieve even higher goals. High Course The High Course is where your group will really learn to look out for one another, encourage and test their nerves 35 feet in the air. Participants can climb a cargo net, a utility pole, or even ascend a rope into the high course. From there, the Balance Beam, Monkey Bridge, 2 Line Traverse, Swinging Vines, and Broken Bridge beckon. After completing all the elements, the Leap of Faith challenges even the most agile and confidant person. After completing the high course, The Rappel Tower beckons. We even can provide you with an “additional challenge” should you want one. "Challenge by Choice" The entire weekend is set up to challenge your unit to do things they never thought possible. We will not, however, force anyone (through peer pressure, or any other measure) to do something they are deathly afraid of. Our staff may ask a participant to try and go one move higher, or take one more step, or try something a different way to help overcome those fears, but the participant has the ultimate say in how far they go. Course Operation Each participant/parent must sign and turn in a Hold Harmless Agreement form to the COPE director in charge of the event as well as Medical forms part A and B. Each COPE program runs from Friday evening arrival through Sunday afternoon. Please contact the Course Director for other options we may be able to provide for your group. Course Director: Tarlin Lanese at Mataguay.COPE@gmail.com

San Diego Imperial Council presents COPE What is Project COPE? COPE is an acronym for Challenging Outdoor Personal Experience and at Mataguay Scout Ranch, we have a weekend that will do just that! Whether your unit needs help learning how to Communicate, Plan, Trust each other, Team-work, build Leadership, learn to Make Decisions, Problem Solve, or just build Self-esteem, we have a program that will fill your unit’s needs. For units that wish to camp as a part of their experience, camping is under the high course and is “backpack” style. Initiative Games Our staff works with your unit through initiative games and objectives that help get everyone in the mood for the day's activities. These "simple" games combined with unit leaders input help identify where your group could use guidance and improvement throughout the weekend. Low Course The Low Course is where your group begins to shine. Through numerous elements (between 18” and 12 feet off the ground) we begin to challenge your group to think outside the box, grow their leadership skills and work cohesively. Each objective builds upon the previous tasks and presents new and exciting challenges. Some groups that enter the program complete all the elements, however most do not. Remember that even if your group has been through a Low Course on previous adventures, we can tailor your weekend to give your unit a chance to achieve even higher goals. High Course The High Course is where your group will really learn to look out for one another, encourage and test their nerves 35 feet in the air. Participants can climb a cargo net, a utility pole, or even ascend a rope into the high course. From there, the Balance Beam, Monkey Bridge, 2 Line Traverse, Swinging Vines, and Broken Bridge beckon. After completing all the elements, the Leap of Faith challenges even the most agile and confidant person. After completing the high course, The Rappel Tower beckons. We even can provide you with an “additional challenge” should you want one. "Challenge by Choice" The entire weekend is set up to challenge your unit to do things they never thought possible. We will not, however, force anyone (through peer pressure, or any other measure) to do something they are deathly afraid of. Our staff may ask a participant to try and go one move higher, or take one more step, or try something a different way to help overcome those fears, but the participant has the ultimate say in how far they go. Course Operation Each participant/parent must sign and turn in a Hold Harmless Agreement form to the COPE director in charge of the event as well as Medical forms part A and B. Each COPE program runs from Friday evening arrival through Sunday afternoon. Please contact the Course Director for other options we may be able to provide for your group. Course Director: Tarlin Lanese at Mataguay.COPE@gmail.com

last.desc: San Diego-Imperial Council presents CANCELLED DUE TO WATER CONDITIONS Kayaking Merit Badge Saturday, November 21, 10:00 am- 3:30 pm Designed for ages 11-17 Scouts will have the opportunity to earn the Kayaking Merit Badge Youth Aquatic Center (1750 Fiesta Island Road) Cost: $36 for youth Lunch is NOT included. You may bring a sack lunch Cost covers boat usage fee's, Lifeguards, and Aquatics Director Check-in opens at 9:45 am Youth must pre-register. NO WALK-IN'S. SCOUTS MUST BE ABLE TO PASS Scouting America SWIM TEST Per the merit badge requirements Scouts are required to pass the BSA swim test before attempting any other requirements. Swim test can be done before your arrival to this event. This can be done the following ways. 1. Have a signed and filled out Scouting America Swim Classification Record Form. 2. Have completed the Swimming and Lifesaving Merit Badge within the last year. 3. Have completed kayaking, canoeing, and or rowing merit badge at summer camp in 2025. Swim test will also be done during the check-in process. We ask parents to stay until the scout has passed the swim test. If a scout can’t pass the test they will be unable to continue in the class. Please send proof of the above to johnathon.hall@scouting.org. If you have any questions, please contact Johnathon. All attending Scouts must bring a Merit Badge application (blue card) with them, signed by their Unit Leader. Blue cards shall not be issued at the event.

Topics include: Adult CPR and The Emergency Action Steps Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and Prioritizing Care Use of Barrier devices… Bleeding Control…Tourniquets Conscious and Unconscious Choking, Burns and Shock Heat and Cold related emergencies and Sudden Illness Injuries to muscles, bones and joints Participants should: be at least 15 years of age (exceptions can be made by training coordinator) be able to complete strenuous activities (such as bending, lifting, kneeling, etc) As a result of the course, participants will complete: First Aid and receive a 2-year card. CPR and receive a 2-year card. This course DOES NOT provide: First aid merit badge - Infant CPR training NOTE: CPR or First Aid may be taken separately but the cost is the same for all or part of a class. last.desc: San Diego Imperial Council and the American Red Cross presents Wilderness and Remote First Aid June 5 & 6, 2027 (Time EACH DAY 9 am - 6 pm - must attend both dates) Camp Balboa, Atherton Hall (1207 Upas St, San Diego 92103) Cost: $100 (includes all training materials) Be prepared for your Wilderness or Philmont Treks. Some of the course topics will include: When Help is delayed: The Emergency Action Steps Emergency Moves and Prioritizing Care Making difficult decisions, causes and prevention of injury Physical exam and report record transfers and evacuations Preventing disease transmission and use of tourniquets Preventing infections, head and spinal injuries Chest and abdominal injuries, burns and shock Hypothermia, major bites and stings And MUCH MORE! Items that will NOT be covered are: survival techniques, CPR training, orienteering or map & compass training Participants need to be at least 15 years of age, have a current adult CPR card prior to attending and be able to complete strenuous activities (such as bending, lifting, kneeling, etc.) Certifications accepted from the following Organizations: American Red Cross Canadian Red Cross American Heart Association National Safety Council American Safety and Health Institute Emergency Care and Safety Institute Medic First Aid San Diego Regional Public Safety Training Institute (Community Colleges Classes) Because of the limited class size, please restrict registrations to only 2 members of a unit or trek (unless class does not fill up)! THIS COURSE IS OPEN TO REGISTERED SCOUTS (at least 15 years old), PARENTS AND LEADERS ONLY!! MUST HAVE A CURRENT CPR CARD (and present at class). Each registrant must have their own email address! Course Materials: Reference Guide, Fact Sheet, Pocket Guide These courses DO NOT apply for any merit badge work. For Questions, please email: stoneboxers1@gmail.com
